release_notes: BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: `DS103` (unresolvable path-like code spans) is now an opt-in rule. By default a scan checks Markdown links and `@`-document mentions only, and the scan notice, `docsentinel rules` and `docsentinel doctor` name `DS103 (set reference_scope = "strict")` as not enabled, so a default scan never reads as if it had checked code-span paths.

Migration: to keep the previous DS103 behaviour set `reference_scope = "strict"` in the configuration or pass `--reference-scope strict` (also accepted by `docsentinel baseline`). Stale `DS103` entries in an existing baseline simply stop matching under the default scope; re-record the baseline (`docsentinel baseline`) to drop them. A `DS103` code span starting with `@` is no longer reported even in strict scope: it belongs to `DS124` and `DS116`.

New rule `DS124` (fast profile, warning, always active): reports a dangling `@`-document mention (`@docs/guide.md` in prose, or a whole inline code span) whose extension is in `at_reference_extensions`. A mention resolves relative to the document, then relative to the link root; `@~/...` and `@/...` mentions are never resolved and a target is never opened. A mention that escapes the scan root is a `DS116` error, not a `DS124` finding. Warnings block only under `--strict`; set `ignore = ["DS124"]` to switch the rule off.

New configuration keys: `reference_scope` (`"links"` default, or `"strict"`) and `at_reference_extensions` (1 to 64 extensions; default md, markdown, mdx, txt, rst, toml, json, yaml, yml, py). New flag: `scan --reference-scope {links,strict}` and `baseline --reference-scope {links,strict}`. `docsentinel doctor` now prints a `reference scope:` line and counts `DS103` among the opt-in rules. See docs/user/reference/configuration.md.

`DS116` now reports three escapes it previously missed, so a scan can gain new errors: a symlink nested inside a symlink's target that points outside the scan root; a symlink pointing outside the root that is reached after more than 64 plain path components; and a committed symlink whose target leaves the root and re-enters it (for example `../out/../root/d`), now a traversal error; a plain link written that way was already reported. `DS101` and `DS113` defer to `DS116` in these cases.

Configuration is now layered: built-in defaults, then a user settings file, then the project configuration (`docsentinel.toml`, `doc_sentinel.toml` or `[tool.doc_sentinel]`), then command-line flags. A key is replaced as a whole value, never merged. `Config` objects passed to `scan()` are still used as given.

JSON project configuration: `docsentinel scan --config FILE.json` (and `baseline --config`) reads a JSON file with the same keys and validation as TOML. JSON is never discovered. It is read strictly: at most 1 MiB, no byte-order mark, no duplicate keys, no `NaN`/`Infinity`, no `null`, a top-level object.

New user settings file: a personal JSON file at `~/.local/share/docsentinel/settings.json` (under `$XDG_DATA_HOME` when set), or at the absolute path in `DOCSENTINEL_SETTINGS`; `DOCSENTINEL_SETTINGS=off` disables it. It cannot set repository-relative options: `baseline`, `include`, `exclude`, `docsig_paths`, `navigation_indexes`, `navigation_required`, `deprecated_references_file`, `report_templates_dir`, `link_root` and `telemetry_domains` are refused with a configuration error (exit code 2).

Permission gate: on POSIX the user settings file, and the directories holding it or a symlink to it, must be owned by you or root and not writable by group or others, or the run exits with code 2 (fix with `chmod go-w`). There is no warning mode. On WSL keep the file in the Linux home, not under `/mnt/c`.

New flags and commands: `docsentinel init --user` creates the starter user settings file (mode 0600, never overwrites, refused when `DOCSENTINEL_SETTINGS=off`); `--no-user-settings` on `scan`, `baseline` and `doctor` ignores the file for one run. `docsentinel doctor` prints `user settings:` and `project config:` lines, and `scan` and `baseline` log an INFO `config:` line naming the sources (option names only). New public API: `load_config_with_sources()` and `ConfigSources`; `load_config()` gained `user_settings=`.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: a literal `include` or `exclude` value (one without `*`, `?` or `[`) now means "this file, or this directory and everything below it", in a configuration file and on the command line. Before, a directory value matched nothing, so `exclude = ["docs/archive"]` silently excluded nothing; now it removes that directory and the walk never enters it. A directory `include` admits only `.md` files. Glob values are unchanged and give the same results as before. A file name containing `*`, `?` or `[` cannot be a literal; select it with a glob such as `notes[[]1].md`.

New flags: `docsentinel scan` and `docsentinel baseline` accept repeatable `--include PATTERN` and `--exclude PATTERN` (a glob, file or directory relative to the scan root, or an absolute path inside it). `--include` replaces the configured `include`; `--exclude` is appended to the configured `exclude`, which still applies; exclude wins. New Python keywords: `docsentinel.scan(root, include=[...], exclude=[...])`, also on top of an injected `Config`. Invoker values are validated before the scan (no `..`, no path outside the scan root, no drive or UNC form, no control characters, at most 256 values of 1,024 characters) and a bad value exits with code 2. An invoker selection that admits no document exits with code 2 (`the selection admitted no document; values are relative to the scan root`) instead of reporting a clean empty scan; an empty selection that comes only from the configuration still exits 0.

`docsentinel doctor` prints `include:` and `exclude:` lines with the pattern counts and their source (the project file or `default`). Each scan logs the effective selection at INFO and warns when an `--include` pattern matches no document or a `--exclude` path does not exist. The argparse abbreviations `--i` and `--ex` are now ambiguous and exit with code 2; write the full flag names. See docs/user/tutorial/cli.md and docs/user/reference/configuration.md.

CI advice: set `DOCSENTINEL_SETTINGS=off` at job level in every CI job that runs `docsentinel`, especially on self-hosted runners, whose home directory can carry a settings file from one job to the next. This repository's own workflow does so.

BREAKING (D1): the default JSON report is now schema 2. `docsentinel scan --format json` emits one record per document, each with its `problems` (rule, type, message, value, line, column, fault class, tier, outcome) and a `domain`; clean documents appear with `problems: []`.
Migration: to keep the previous schema-1 bytes exactly, use `docsentinel scan --format json-v1`. `--format json-documents` is the bare per-document list.

Every report is now rendered from a JSON template over a JSON-shaped context built by the new `telemetry/` package; nothing about the layout is hardcoded. Packaged templates: `text`, `github`, `json`, `json-v1`, `json-documents`. The text report prints findings directly under their document and hides clean documents (`--show-clean-documents` or `report_show_clean_documents` shows them); the GitHub report adds `col` and `title=<rule>`.

New: `scan --template PATH` renders your own template; `scan --format NAME` also accepts templates from `report_templates_dir`, which fails closed (exit 2) for every format if it is unreadable or escapes the scan root. New config options: `report_templates_dir`, `report_show_clean_documents`, `report_include_run_meta`. See docs/user/tutorial/custom-reports.md.

New extension API: `--extension builtin:domain` labels each document (`telemetry_domains`, first match wins, default `docs`; at most 256 rules, 4096 glob characters in total) and `builtin:document_stats` adds problem density. Domain labels are asserted by the scanned repository, not verified.

`python:<module>:<callable>` extensions are accepted from the command line only (never from configuration, where one is a ConfigError) and only with `--allow-python-extensions` or `DOCSENTINEL_ALLOW_PYTHON_EXTENSIONS=1`. An admitted extension runs with full trust (it is not a sandbox) and the origin check is point-in-time. Do not set the variable for a whole workflow or job, in `pull_request_target` workflows, `.envrc` or pre-commit args. In GitHub Actions use `--format github`.
Not included: the Milestone 0006 fault-event adapter, `telemetry_sink` and FaultEvent emission are not implemented in this release.
Configuration discovery now accepts both docsentinel.toml and doc_sentinel.toml as the standalone config file; docsentinel.toml remains the preferred name.
Having both standalone files in one scan root is ambiguous and fails closed with a ConfigError (exit code 2) naming both files.
`docsentinel init` still creates docsentinel.toml but refuses to run next to an existing doc_sentinel.toml.
Documentation updated (configuration reference, tutorials, architecture, README) and new unit, integration and mock tests cover both names.
First stable release of DocSentinel, a deterministic-first documentation QA framework and Python library with one engine behind the CLI, the Python API and the pytest plugin.

Fast profile (stdlib only): DS101 dangling links/anchors, DS102 stray HTML comments, DS103 unresolvable path-like code spans, DS104 conflicting heading/explicit anchors, DS105 heading hierarchy, DS106 empty sections, DS108 reference-style link integrity, DS109 malformed/unclosed code fences, DS113 missing local assets, DS114 duplicate document identifiers, DS116 path traversal outside the documentation root, DS117 malformed GFM tables.

Opt-in policy rules, inert until configured: DS110 fence language labels (require_fence_languages), DS112 navigation integrity (navigation_indexes), DS115 deprecated names and migrated references (deprecated_references_file), DS118 file and directory naming (documentation_naming).

Standard profile (docsentinel[standard]): DS201 text complexity, DS202 duplicated text, DS203 low-information content, DS204 docstring-to-signature mismatch, with separate baseline and CI lanes and lazy loading of heavy dependencies.

Deep profile (docsentinel[deep]): DS301 fact-contradiction candidates; heuristic, advisory-only (exit code 0) and gated behind an explicit opt-in (deep_confirm, --i-understand-deep-is-heuristic or DOCSENTINEL_DEEP_CONFIRM=1).
Layered configuration via doc_sentinel.toml or [tool.doc_sentinel] in pyproject.toml, with typed and validated policy options, rule selection by code or prefix, and SHA-256 fingerprint baselines.

CLI commands scan, baseline, init, rules and doctor; text, JSON (schema v1) and GitHub Actions output; exit codes 0 (clean), 1 (blocking findings), 2 (config or scan failure); pre-commit hooks for the fast and standard profiles.
Security hardening: control, bidi and zero-width characters are neutralised in text and GitHub annotation output, and path handling is contained to the scan root with symlink-escape protection.
Packaging: release tooling (release-saga) and flakeforge are declared as dependencies; wheels and sdists are built with hatchling and requires Python 3.12+.
